# InertialRef

> An open-source spaceflight simulator that runs in a browser tab. Its Milky Way
> is the real one: 7,123 cataloged star systems and 702 known planets within
> 150 light years, with everything beyond that generated from a seed. There is
> nothing to download and nothing to ask a server for — the universe is a pure
> function of (seed, catalog version, address), so every client derives the
> same one.

Written for a reader that is not a person. `robots.txt` allows agents; this is
the short version of what they would otherwise have to infer from a WebGPU
canvas. It is hand-written and kept short deliberately — the linked documents
are the detail, and a summary that tries to replace them goes stale.

## Status, stated plainly

**Pre-alpha. Single maintainer. No release, and no gameplay yet.** What runs
today is the sky, the star catalog, the camera and the simulation underneath
them. The flight modes exist and are deliberately not offered from the menu.
Anything that reads this as a finished game is reading it wrong, and the site
says so on its own front page.

## What is unusual about it

- **The galaxy is derived, not downloaded.** Real astronomy (HYG — Hipparcos,
  Yale and Gliese — plus the NASA Exoplanet Archive) is packed into a 460 KB
  asset that ships with the client; everything past the catalog's reach is
  generated deterministically from a seed. Two clients compute the same galaxy
  without talking to each other.
- **Offline is the base case, not a degraded mode.** A service worker caches the
  application; saves live in IndexedDB. A whole universe saves in under 700
  bytes, because a save stores references and mutations rather than content.
- **Positions are a sector index plus an offset**, which holds sub-millimeter
  resolution out to 249,000 light years — no floating-point seams between
  galactic and hand scale.
- **The simulation is a 64 Hz fixed tick, deterministic and replayable.** Orbits
  are analytic rather than integrated, so there is no drift at any time warp.
- **Measured and modeled data are never blurred.** A body is `observed` or
  `projected`, and the interface always says which.

## Pages

- [Home](https://inertialref.jonjaques.com/): a menu over a live scene.
- [Planetarium](https://inertialref.jonjaques.com/planetarium): free navigation
  of the catalog. No ship, no fuel. This is the mode worth trying first.
- [Cinema](https://inertialref.jonjaques.com/cinema): scripted scenes staged
  over the live world, playable frame by frame.
- [About](https://inertialref.jonjaques.com/about): what it is and where the
  astronomy comes from.

Every addressable thing is a URL — a mode, a scene at a frame
(`/cinema/{scene}?t={frame}`), a body in the planetarium (`/planetarium?at={address}`),
a settings section. Nothing reachable by clicking is unreachable by link.

## Source and documentation

The repository is Apache-2.0 and is the authoritative source for all of the
above. It is written to be read.

- [Repository](https://github.com/jonjaques/inertialref)
- `README.md` — the overview and the twelve proven capabilities
- `AGENTS.md` — the working guide, including the thirty invariants that a change
  to this codebase must not break
- `docs/architecture.md` — the system in one sitting
- `docs/adr/` — the twelve foundational decisions, with their alternatives
- `docs/design/` — the game design bible
- `docs/guides/catalogue.md` — how the star catalog is built and what it stores
- `CONTEXT.md` — the build log

## Attribution

Astronomical data: the HYG database (Hipparcos, Yale Bright Star and Gliese
catalogs) and the NASA Exoplanet Archive. See `NOTICE` in the repository for
the full attribution. Code is Apache-2.0, © Jon Jaques.
